page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-16 belongs to the general-purpose compute family and runs on the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs coupled with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Because the CPU allocation is dedicated rather than shared or burstable, it guarantees consistent core access across computing cycles.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local disk storage, which means the instance relies on remote persistent storage volumes for operating system installation and data persistence. The instance also features zero GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, keeping the footprint focused on standard CPU-bound operations without specialized hardware add-ons.

The 16-core arm64 environment delivers a balanced resource footprint for enterprise workloads designed to run on ARM platforms. The architecture is suited for containerized services, web serving layers, microservices, application backends, and continuous integration workflows. Systems requiring massive direct-attached disk throughput or machine learning hardware acceleration will need to accommodate the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs.

The instance configuration includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for system and persistent data volumes. Additionally, the configuration features zero GPU accelerators and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Operating on ARM-based dedicated computing resources, the n4a-standard-16 is suited for multi-threaded general enterprise workloads, container clusters, microservices, application hosting, and continuous integration environments optimized for ARM platforms. Workloads requiring extreme storage throughput or specialized hardware acceleration must account for the lack of local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs.
